abstract: A photonic crystal fiber based polarizer, capable to work at two communication windows of around 1310 nm and 1550 nm concurrently in which plasmonics plays an important role to achieve filtering characteristics, is reported. Based on the numerical outcomes the loss magnitude for y- and x-polarized modes are about 1014 dB/cm and 0.05 dB/cm, respectively, at 1310 nm meaning that y-polarized light is 20812 times lossy than that of x-polarized case. In addition, at the wavelength of 1550 nm, the loss of x-polarized light is 6439 times lower than the y-polarized light which makes the structure as polarization filter at second window as well. The promising filtering characteristics of the proposed structure may find applications in two communication windows at the same time.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Segmentation and Classification using Spatial Fuzzy C mean and Quadratic Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Electrical, Computer & Telecommunication Engineering (ICECTE)
abstract: Precise detection and classification of brain tumors at a reasonable time is vital to enhance the survival of a patient. But due to the big dimensional and anatomical diversity between brain tumors, this is a difficult job. In this contribution, we are proposing an improved spatial fuzzy c-mean (SFCM) for brain tumor segmentation and a quadratic support vector machine (QSVM) for tumor type classification. When applied to the BraTS 2018 dataset, the acquired segmentation outcomes were shown to be 7.16% and 12.78% better than the conventional fuzzy c-mean (FCM) and k-mean. This method assists radiologists in understanding the medical image and gives a second opinion.

articleTitle: C-V characteristics of high performance Si3N4/GaOxN1−x/GaN double gate MIS-HEMT
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Electrical, Computer & Telecommunication Engineering (ICECTE)
abstract: Closed-form solution for electrostatics in a quantum well heterostructure like Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>/GaO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>/GaN DG MIS-HEMT, working in the nanometer regime is highly non-linear due to strong Quantum Mechanical(QM) effects. Numerical simulation is most effective to predict the characteristics. Self-consistent simulation with couple Schrodinger's and Poisson's equations are used in this work to get quantum capacitance vs gate voltage (C-V) characteristics. In this particular design of DG MIS-HEMT, staircase-like behavior of CV characteristics found. Because of the use of GaO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub> layer, C-V characteristics show less steeper staircase behavior. The effects of different parameters like channel thickness, doping concentration on the CV curve have also been explored here.

articleTitle: A Comparative analysis of appearance based subspace methods for facial expression recognition
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Electrical, Computer & Telecommunication Engineering (ICECTE)
abstract: Facial expression recognition is like a pattern recognition problem, which is divided into two parts dimensionality reduction and classification. It is very much challenging to find out an efficient combination of dimensionality reduction technique and classifier. Many appearance based dimensionality reduction techniques have been proposed in recent years. This research focuses on the comparative analysis of appearance based subspace methods (PCA, KPCA, PCA+MI, KPCA+MI) for facial expression recognition in completely equal working conditions. PCA is a vastly used feature extraction technique which is linear and unsupervised. A kernelized version of PCA is called KPCA increases classification accuracy by handling non-linear data which is an unsupervised feature extraction method. KPCA shows the highest accuracy among these two methods. Combining a feature selection method MI with KPCA which can highly increase the recognition rate. The accuracy of KPCA+MI was above 95.24% when the moderate number of training features were used to train the SVM with RBF kernel.

articleTitle: Channel Characterization at mmWave Band Inside High Speed Water Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Electrical, Computer & Telecommunication Engineering (ICECTE)
abstract: Wireless telecommunication systems with upcoming and advanced technology standards and higher bandwidth is expected to mitigate demand of users and reduce end-to-end delay. Marine environments are still not explored and communication ways are not so fast comparative to other scenarios. With forthcoming technology 5G and mmWave, maritime channels are need to be explored for more research opportunities and development with advanced mobile communications. From this motivation, this research is based on investigation of comparative analysis of power delay profiles, path loss characteristics in maritime channels considering 38, 60 and 73 GHz of mmWave. 60 GHz is the license free spectrum and suitable for short distance communication, water attenuation is minimum in 38 GHz and 73 GHz theoretically provides higher bandwidth, these factors are considered in this work. In this study, various delay spread, signal strength deviation at receiving end, loss exponents, delay parameters, signal-to-noise ratio are surveyed for both direct line sight (LOS) and Non-direct visual sight (NLOS) conditions, such parameters define channel impulse responses in wireless maritime channels, inside high speed water vehicle. This study will provide channel characteristics in specific scenarios and further research direction in various aspects in this area.

articleTitle: Optimization of Visible Light Intensity from Upconversion Nanoparticles (UCNPs) under 980 nm Pump
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Electrical, Computer & Telecommunication Engineering (ICECTE)
abstract: Visible light is considered very promising for medical applications. Green light at 550 nm wavelength can be obtained using lanthanide-doped up-conversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) such as Erbium (Er). In this work, we analyzed optical characteristics and potentiality of Er to generate improved light at 550 nm utilizing the non-linear spectral mechanisms: up-conversion (UC) and excited state absorption (ESA) under 980 nm pump. To improve the intensity of 550 nm emission, co- doping with Ytterbium (Yb) has been investigated and found to be useful. We observed that adequate amount of Yb enhances visible emission intensity of Er through energy transfer process from Yb to Er under 980 nm pump, which can be used for improving visible emission in lifesaving medical applications.

articleTitle: Polarization Beam Splitter on Metal Nanowires Filled Micro-structured Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Electrical, Computer & Telecommunication Engineering (ICECTE)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a polarization splitter based on a dual-core square lattice photonic crystal fiber with selectively metal-filled air holes. The use of metal nanowires adds plasmonic characteristics to the structure that helps the splitter to maintain extinction ratio (ER) higher than 20 dB over a wide bandwidth of about 500 nm (1400 nm to 1900 nm). The splitter shows best performance at 1.55 μm of wavelength with the highest ER of 109.57 dB. The proposed splitter is able to split the incoming light into two orthogonal polarized rays at a short length of 90.73 μm and can be a versatile device for sensing applications and optical networks.

articleTitle: A Communicative Computer Generated Hologram for Security in Communication System Using Fraunhofer Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Electrical, Computer & Telecommunication Engineering (ICECTE)
abstract: In this work, we developed a Computer-Generated Hologram (CGH) based on Fraunhofer algorithm using Matlab for making a relatively secured communication system. In the Fraunhofer algorithm, the computation of far-field amplitude is carried out through Fourier transform which is required to calculate the interference pattern of digital holograms. Here the communicative holograms are developed by means of adding the far-field amplitude of main object image and reference object image. The reconstruction of the main object image is also accomplished the use of this algorithm. We detect the image overlapping constraints in the output image and additionally find the technique to avoid the overlapping between the main object image and inverted main object image at the receiver side. According to the properties of the hologram, the decoding of transmitted hologram is nearly impossible except reference information, so the proposed communicative holographic machine can be applied in the area of secure communication.

articleTitle: K-mer Based DNA Methylation Status Prediction Using Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Electrical, Computer & Telecommunication Engineering (ICECTE)
abstract: Cancer, diabetics, cardiovascular diseases and some of rare diseases are occurred due to the modification in human genome. DNA methylation is one of such type of genomic change. When one or more methyl groups are added to the DNA molecule, it is termed as DNA methylation. It is very difficult and challenging to deal with DNA methylation because of having high dimentionality and noisiness of methylation dataset. In this research work, we have proposed a machine learning based computational model for predicting DNA methylation. Our model is highly involved with bioinformatics and genomic information to extract genomic features. All previous works regarding the prediction of DNA methylation were only based on the statistical tools. Our model has two phases including the feature extraction and selection phase and the classification phase. In feature extraction phase we have used k-mer bioinformatics algorithm to extract the most appropriate features. Then using some statistical tools, we have selected the most discriminating features. Finally, we have chosen SVM, a supervised machine learning algorithm to predict the DNA methylation status. Our model has produced a classification accuracy of 98.65%.
